title: Tell Me If I Am Disturbing You
text:
Tell me if I am disturbing you,

he said as he came in,

because I will leave immediately.

You are not only disturbing me,

I answered,

you are turning my whole existence upside down.

Welcome.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Kilpi's conversational timing and the final reversal into welcome.

title: When You Have Seen a Cloud
editorial_note: The source includes a Spanish translation credit to Luis López Nieves; the English rendering preserves the quiet lake image.

title: What Is This Noise That Wakes Me at Night?
text:
What is this noise that wakes me at night?


It is biology, demanding its rights.

At night it is heard better,

clearly, when the

sociologists are asleep.
editorial_note: The source includes a Spanish translation credit to Luis López Nieves; the English keeps the poem's dry biological punchline.

title: Well, If You Really
text:
Well, if you really

want a confession,

here it is:

I have had thirty-six lovers.

Well, yes. You are right...

that is too many.

Thirty-five would have been enough.

But, darling, the thirty-sixth

is you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the comic setup and the intimate snap of the last two lines.

title: As I Go to Sleep, I Think
text:
As I go to sleep, I think:

tomorrow I will heat the sauna,

pamper myself,

walk, swim, wash,

invite myself to evening tea,

speak to myself in a friendly

and admiring way, praising myself:

Brave little woman,

I believe in you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the self-care list plain and lets the final encouragement stay simple.
